== Biography ==
:1870 Census, Franklinsville, Randolph County, North Carolina
:Anna Giles F 70
:Malinda Brown F 22 Domestic
(Next household)
:William Glassgo M 26
:Martha J Glassgo F 24
:Arganna S Glassgo F 1

:1880 Census, Franklinsville, Randolph County, North Carolina
:Luke Cross M 66
:Lucinda Cross F 61
:Alfins Cross M 16 Grandson
:Malinda Brown F 31 Servant (Housekeeper)
:John R Brown M 7 Boarder
:Minnie F Brown F 3 Boarder

The census indicates that John and Minnie's father was born in Tennessee, but subsequent censuses do not agree with this and all say North Carolina. 

:1900 Census, Franklinville, Randolph County, North Carolina
:Melinda Brown F 52 North Carolina
:Mary Brown F 15 North Carolina
:Daniel P Brown M 12 North Carolina

Malinda was listed as the head of household on the 1900 Federal Census. She was educated, and she was working as a washer woman in Franklinville, Randolph County, North Carolina. Daniel's 15 year old sister, Mary, was working in a cotton mill and 12 year old Daniel was attending school.

On December 18, 1908, in Randolph County, Malinda married William Julian Glasgow. Malinda worked for one William Glassco's mother-in-law back in 1870. This marriage occurred shortly after Martha J Giles Glassco's death. Hmmm...

:1910 Census, Greensboro Road, Liberty, Randolph County, North Carolina
:William Glascoe M 68
:Melinda Glascoe F 65

The census appears to indicate that this is William's second marriage and Malinda's first. William was born in Virginia, as were his parents. William was a veteran of the confederate army. (But it's very complicated. He was a deserter who eventually defected to the union side. I'll post more if I can ever confirm that he is the father of Malinda's children. People seem pretty convinced that he was John R H Brown's father, at least. Maybe there are family stories. One relative said she has seen a bastardy bond indicating William fathered Daniel, too.)

William's death certificate indicates that he died on 1/19/1916 from chronic Bright's disease. This does differ from the date of death on his tombstone. It states that he was a widowed farmer, his father is Jesse Glasgow born in Virginia, and his mother is Martha Davis born in Randolph County, North Carolina.
